name: Chor Voli
description: Chor Voli is a traditional Afghan partition card game where players divide their 13-card hands into up to four 3-card combinations, similar to Brag hands. These combinations are then played out in a series of showdowns starting with each player's strongest hand. The game is related to the British game Crash and the Pakistani variant Ramchi.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Afghanistan
Time Period: 20th century
Historical Development: Learned by Gyula Zsigri from Sherzod Lukmoni in 1992. A similar game called Ramchi was described in 2011 by Tilman Schieber, said to have come from Pakistan where it is popular with Afghan refugees.
Cultural Significance: Played in Afghanistan and by Afghan refugee communities in Pakistan.
timeline: 1992: Game documented by Gyula Zsigri from Sherzod Lukmoni
2011: Similar game Ramchi described by Tilman Schieber from Pakistan
Present: Played in Afghanistan and Afghan refugee communities
history.cultural: Chor Voli represents traditional Afghan card gaming culture. The game is played counterclockwise, following regional customs. It serves as entertainment and social bonding within Afghan communities.
history.evolution: The game appears to have evolved within Afghan culture, with the Pakistani variant Ramchi developing among Afghan refugee communities. The partition game mechanic is similar to British Crash.

rules.objective: Win chips from the pool by forming stronger 3-card combinations than opponents. The player with the highest four of a kind (if dealt) wins all four chips immediately.
rules.gameplay:
1. Before deal: Each player contributes 1 chip to the pool
2. Deal: 13 cards to each player
3. If a player has four of a kind: No play occurs; highest four of a kind wins all 4 chips
4. Otherwise: Players sort hands into up to four 3-card combinations
5. Discard face down any cards not part of valid combinations (each card used in only one combination)
6. Showdowns occur in order: strongest combination first, then second strongest, etc.
7. Winner of each showdown takes 1 chip from the pool
keyRules: Three-card combinations rank (high to low): Three of a kind, Running flush (3-card straight flush), Run (3-card straight), Flush (3 cards same suit), Three unrelated cards
Three unrelated cards must have no suit connection and no pair - if two cards share a suit or form a pair, they cannot be 'unrelated'
Each card can only be used in one combination
Unused cards are discarded face down and do not play
Four of a kind ends the hand immediately with that player winning
Combinations compared using standard Brag hand rankings

strategy.basic: Learn the hand rankings thoroughly. Understand that three unrelated cards must truly be unrelated (no shared suits, no pairs).
strategy.intermediate: The key skill is deciding how to divide your 13 cards into combinations. Avoid making one very strong combination and three weak ones. Try to create balanced strength across all four combinations.
strategy.advanced: More profitable to make the first combination only slightly stronger than the second, and so on, because later rounds are equally valuable to win. Consider opponent tendencies and potential holdings when partitioning your hand.
tips: Balance your combinations - don't put all strength in one hand
Later rounds are just as valuable as early rounds
Consider what cards opponents might hold when partitioning
Sometimes sacrificing one combination can strengthen others
Pay attention to how opponents partition their hands for future reads
